name: Captions (Live)
explanation: This criterion applies to live audio content delivered through synchronized media — a live-streamed webinar, a live news broadcast, or a live-captioned video call. You must provide real-time captions that are synchronized with the spoken audio as it happens. This is the live counterpart to captions for prerecorded video. Because the content hasn't been produced in advance, captions can't be authored ahead of time and checked for accuracy — they have to be generated as the broadcast happens, typically through a live captioning service or automatic speech recognition. The bar for accuracy is necessarily lower than prerecorded captions, but captions must still be present and reasonably track what's being said. This does not apply to live audio that isn't part of synchronized media, such as a plain audio-only phone call.
whoItAffects: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users watching a live stream have no way to perceive spoken audio in real time without captions. Unlike prerecorded video, they can't pause and check a transcript afterward if they want to follow along as it happens. People joining a live event in a sound-off or noisy environment, like watching a company all-hands from a shared office, rely on live captions to follow along. Non-native speakers of the broadcast's language, and some users with cognitive or learning disabilities, benefit from reading captions alongside fast or accented live speech that's harder to process by ear alone.
howToTest: Join a live stream or webinar that has spoken audio, and look for a visible captions control in the player. Turn captions on and confirm that text appears on screen while people are speaking, with only a short delay. Watch for a minute or two to check that captions keep pace with new speech instead of freezing or falling behind. It fails if there's no caption option offered, or if captions stop updating partway through.

check.question: A company hosts a live all-hands webinar with a presenter speaking over live video. According to SC 1.2.4, what is required?
choices: A transcript of the webinar posted to the company wiki after it ends
Real-time synchronized captions of the spoken audio as the webinar happens
Nothing, since live events are exempt from captioning requirements
A sign-language interpreter window is required instead of captions
